classification.difficultyReason: Use the fixed area to eliminate one dimension and count external and internal fencing to form an objective function.

content.prompt:
A rectangular enclosure of area $288\,\mathrm{m}^2$ is to be divided into three equal pens by two internal fences parallel to one side. Let the external width (perpendicular to the dividers) be $x$ metres.

Show that the equation for the total fencing is $F=2x+\frac{1152}{x}$.

spec.description: An unlabelled rectangle divided into three equal horizontal strips by two solid horizontal fences. All boundaries are black and the regions are unfilled.
spec.mathematics: The external width x is perpendicular to the dividers. There are two external widths and four lengths of fencing.
spec.answerVisibility: No calculated dimensions or answers are shown.

answer.worked:
Let the length of the enclosure be $\ell$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}x\ell&=288\\\ell&=\frac{288}{x}\end{align*}$$
The total fencing comprises two widths and four lengths, including the two internal fences.
$$\begin{align*}F&=2x+4\ell\\F&=2x+4\left(\frac{288}{x}\right)\\F&=2x+\frac{1152}{x}\end{align*}$$
Here $F$ is measured in metres.
